FIFA's seeding system places De la Fuente's side in the same half of the bracket as France, making a semi-final between them a likely scenario if both top their group - that would take place at MetLife Stadium on July 19.

Spain are joint outright favourites alongside France. They arrive as reigning European champions, ranked second in the world by FIFA, and unbeaten in 33 matches since a competitive loss to Scotland in March 2023. The key concerns are the fitness of Rodri and Lamine Yamal, and Spain's record of failing to win a single World Cup knockout game since lifting the trophy in 2010. If both star players are fit and at their best in the knockout rounds, Spain have a strong case as the tournament's most complete side.
